Title: Fabric Kit Manual
Content: 1. COMPONENTS Please identify and confirm the following components. SCALE UTILITY KNIFE SCREWDRIVER CHARGING ADAPTER USER MANUAL 2. TOOL LEGEND BENDING TEST DEVICE STRETCH TEST DEVICE 3. SPECIFICATION 4. HOW TO ATTACH THE DIGITAL FORCE GAUGE TO THE FABRIC KIT Use total of eight screws to assemble. Remaining two screws are extra. Screw the Jig into the Digital Force Gauge. Turn about 3-4 times and do not tighten all the way. However screw the Jig until the Control Lever faces up, aligning with the Digital Force Gauge. Align the Holder underneath the Digital Force Gauge. Fasten the Holder to the Digital Force Gauge with Screws (x4). Loosely tighten the Screws (x4) to affix the Digital Force Gauge to the Fabric Kit, enough so that Digital Force Gauge can be moved. Shift the Digital Force Gauge to align the Jig as the image below vertically. Tighten Screw B to affix the Digital Force Gauge Holder to the Fabric Kit. If the Digital Force Gauge is not affixed properly, the measured Force values may not be accurate. 5. OVERVIEW Prepare fabrics Measure the fabric weight and thickness Measure the bending strength Measure the stretch Calculate entered measurements Apply a texture 6. HOW TO MAKE FABRIC Launch CLO Enterprise, then switch to Emulator mode using the top-right drop-down menu to enter the values measured from the Fabric Kit. A. SWATCH PREPARATION Before cutting out the swatches, please ironing the swatch gently without causing any shrinkage. Confirm the grainline of the fabric. Prepare a total of three swatches with the provided stencil. Each swatch will represent a different grain, cut in the (1) weft, (2) warp, and (3) bias directions, measuring 220mm x 30mm in size. These will be used to measure the weight, bending, and stretch properties of the fabric. Cut the swatches along the drawn guidelines, being as precise as possible for accurate measurements. B. FABRIC WEIGHT Turn on the scale. Place all three swatches on the scale. Enter the displayed weight in the Emulator. C. FABRIC THICKNESS Press the lever of the thickness gauge to create a gap and place the swatch. Place the 220mm x 30mm swatch in between the gap. Release the lever and enter the measured thickness to the Emulator. Click Next to continue. D. BENDING TEST The Bending Test is performed 3 times : first for the weft swatch, and next the warp swatch, then the last for the bias swatch. Slide open the 1-1 Ruler of the Bending Test device. Turn the 1-2 Clamp back, then insert the end of the swatch, lining it up to the dotted line. Pull down the 1-2 Clamp to affix the swatch. Wind the 1-4 Control Lever clockwise, then stop when the fabric hits the ground. Measure and enter this point of contact as the Contact Distance (A). Place the 1-1 Ruler beneath the swatch, then enter the measured length (B) in the Emulator. E. STRETCH TEST The stretch test will allow you to measure the stretchability and threshold at which a fabric will no longer stretch. To do this you will explore the relationship between length of stretch and force applied to the fabric, then record and input your findings into the Emulator Mode of CLO. The reading from the Length Ruler and Digital Force Gauge combined will be one set of measurements. You will need a minimum of 3 sets and a maximum of 5 sets for each swatch. When testing, you will need to determine, which unit of length will be your constant. Wind the Control Lever until the needle aligns with 0 on the Length Ruler. Loosen the Clamps at each end of the Fabric Bed. Insert both ends of the swatch between the Jig openings, aligning the 10mm line marks. Tighten the Clamps at each end to secure the swatch ends. Turn on the Digital Force Gauge. Determine Length constant: We recommend you to fill out all five sections as possible because when you have more measurements, data is more accurate. When the swatch is pulled by 1mm and the force is less than 0.01kgf 1) Pull the fabric swatch until the force value is 0.01kgf. 2) Starting with the length reached at step 1, check the length and force of each 10mm increment. 3) Record 10 sections. (In the case of not being able to record 10 sections, record all the measurable sections.) 4) Use a value only when the force difference of each section is at least 0.02kgf. (If the force difference for each interval is less than 0.02kgf, do not use that value.) 5) Finally, select and use values resulted in at least 3 sections and up to 5 sections. (We recommend that you fill out all five sections as much as possible because the more measurements you have, the more accurate the data is.). When the swatch is pulled by 1 mm and the force value is over 0.01kgf 1) Check the value of the force when the swatch is pulled to 1mm. 2) Starting with the length reached at step 1, check the length and force of each 1mm increments. 3) At this time, measure 3 to 5 sections. (We recommend that you ll out all ve sections as much as possible because the more measurements you have, the more accurate the data is) Once the test has been completed for a swatch, reset the Control Lever so the needle aligns with 0 on the Length Ruler. Then unscrew the clamp at each end and remove the swatch. If you are finished testing you can turn the Digital Force Gauge off. In between each swatch test you should turn the digital force gauge off and then back on after the needle has been returned to the 0 marks. Click Next to Continue. 7. HOW TO USE THE DIGITAL FORCE GAUGE The Digital Force Gauge uses the default settings as the image below. If a button was mistakenly pushed, power the Digital Force Gauge off, then on, to reset the device to its default settings. However, if the default unit of measurement was changed, press button B to reset the device to Kgf. FREQUENTLY USED BUTTONS A. POWER - turn the Digital Force Gauge on/off C. LED - turn the LED display on/off D. UNIT - change the unit of measurement Kgf is used to measure the stretch FREQUENTLY USED BUTTONS The following buttons are not used in the Stretch Test. If one of these buttons are mistakenly pushed, reset the Digital Force Gauge with the Power button. B. RESET E. MODE F. REVIEW G. SETTINGS I. SAVE CHARGING Use the provided adapter to charge the Digital Force Gauge.

Title: 3D vs Real-life Sample Comparison Guide
Content: Download our 3D vs Real-life Sample Comparison Guide that addresses important check-list needed when comparing 3D and real-life samples.

Title: Render in CLOSET
Content: Render in CLOSET - Render 3D Garments in CLOSET regardless of users computer specification. - Main MenuRender Render via CLOSET - Main Menu ShareRender via CLOSET - Main MenuFile Share Render via CLOSET - You are navigated to CLOSET.

Title: Reset Bounding Volumes (ver4.2.0)
Content: Objective Reset Bounding Volumes to the original placement after adjustments. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes Bounding Volumes are replaced to their original placements.

Title: 3D Garment Information (ver4.1.0 and Above)
Content: List of Contents Enter Default Garment Information Add Category Reorder Category Delete Category Objective Write and check important Garment information. Location Main Menu File Information Garment Operation Enter Default Garment Information Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Information Garment The Garment Information window appears. Four categories: StyleNumber, Name, Description, Fabric, Colorway, and Size appear by default. Click the Edit icon on the right top corner of the window. The Garment Information window changed to the edit mode. Type in necessary information next to each category and click OK. Typed in information is saved. Add Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click the Add icon. A category is added. Click the drop-down menu and select desired category. There are eleven categories to choose from: StyleNumber, Name, Description, Fabric, Colorway, Size, Category, Memo, SizeMemo, Price, and SizeChart. Type in necessary information for each category and click OK. Typed in information is saved. Reorder Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode.. Click and drag the category to the desired position. The category is moved to where the mouse is released. When categories are re-ordered completely, click OK. Revised category order is saved. Delete Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click the Delete icon next to each category. The selected category is deleted. When the editing is completed, click OK. The deleted category no longer appears in the Garment Information window. Note: Toggle on Display When Garment File Loads option to open the Garment Information window every time the file opens. Open or save Garment information such as categories, order, and contents by using the Open and Save buttons on the right top corner of the edit mode. Use the Default File setting to designate default Garment Information file.

Title: Fasten Button
Content: List of Contents Fasten Button Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes Unfastening Buttons and Buttonholes Fasten Button - Fasten buttons and buttonholes on 3D Garment. - Select the Fasten Button tool from the 3D Toolbar. Fastening Buttons and Buttonholes Fasten a Single Pair - Select the Fasten Button tool from the 3D Toolbar. - The 3D Garment will turn translucent and both buttons and buttonholes can be easily identified. - Either in the 2D or the 3D Window, click on the button to be fastened. - Then, click on the buttonhole that the button will be fastened to. - The selected button and the buttonhole will be fastened when the Simulation is activated as the button simulates above the buttonhole. - If the selected button and the buttonhole are fastened properly, a lock icon will hover over the button. Fasten Multiple Pairs - To fasten multiple buttons at once, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass all buttons to be fastened. - Click the first buttonhole of the collection which selected buttons are paired. Unfastening Buttons and Buttonholes Unfasten a Singe Pair - Select the Fasten Button tool from the 3D Toolbar. - The 3D Garment will turn translucent and both buttons and buttonholes can be easily identified. - Select on the button or buttonhole to be unfastened either in the 2D or the 3D Window. - The lock icon will disappear and the Garment will simulate unfastened. Unfasten Multiple Pairs - To unfasten multiple pairs of buttons and buttonholes, click and drag on the 2D window to select all buttons to be unfastened. - Selected buttons are unfastened at once.

Title: Edit 2D Seam Allowance Properties
Content: List of Contents Seam Allowance Properties Edit Seam Allowance Properties Seam Allowance Properties - Edit properties of seam allowances as needed. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Create Seam Allowance - Select the Seam Allowance tool from the 2D toolbar. Edit Seam Allowance Properties - Select the Pattern outline or the Internal Line of the seam allowance to be edited. - The seam allowance is selected and its Pattern outline or Internal Line is highlighted. - The selected seam allowances properties appear in the Property Editor. Width - Modify the width of the seam allowance as needed. Seam Type - Choose the seam type of a seam allowances start, end, and intersection. - Options are activated or deactivated depending on the selected point. Start - This option activates when only one seam allowance is created on either end of the selected segment. - Choose the desired type of the seam among three options. End - This option activates when only one seam allowance is created on either end of the selected segment. - Choose the desired type of the seam among three options. Intersection - This option activates when seam allowances are created on both ends of the selected segment. - Choose the desired type of the seam among six options.

Title: V-Ray Render
Content: List of Contents V-Ray Render Interactive Render Stop Render Final Render (Image/Video) V-Ray Render - Produce more vivid and photorealistic images with clear seamlines and puckerings. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select Render Render - Or, navigate to the Main Menu Display Window Render Interactive Render - By default, the Stop Render tool is activated when the Render window opens. - Click the Interactive Render tool on the 2D toolbar or click the message, Click here to start the Interactive Render to start rendering. - Render Garments and Avatars in the 3D window in real-time with the Interactive Render tool. - Any changes in 3D view are also reflected in the Render window. Stop Render - Click the Stop Render tool to temporarily pause while rendering. - Rendering is paused in the Render window. - Any changes in the 3D window do not reflect in the Render window when the Stop Render tool is activated. - Click the Interactive Render tool to resume real time rendering. Final Render (Image/Video) - The image shown in the Render window is a preview of real time Render, which Render settings are not fully applied. - To extract the final Render images or a video with Render settings fully applied, click the Final Render (Image/Video) tool. - The progress of the rendering appears on the right top corner of the Render toolbar. - When rendering is completed, the Information window appears, informing the images or video have been saved. - Select the Open the Folder button to open the folder where the final output is saved. - The final output is automatically saved to the saving path assigned in the Image/Video Properties. - Image/Video Properties, Light Properties, and Render Properties are fully applied to the final render output.

Title: Transform Pattern
Content: List of Contents Transform Pattern Select Pattern Select Multiple Patterns Move Pattern Scale Pattern Rotate Pattern Transform Pattern - Select, move, and scale Patterns. - Select the Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Edit Tranform Pattern. Select Pattern Click - Click within the pattern to be selected. - Or, create a marquee box to encompass the Patterns to be selected. Keep in mind that the Patterns need to be fully enclosed within the marquee box in order to be selected properly. Lasso Selection - Double click on the 2D window to activate the Lasso Selection. - Click around the Patterns to be selected to draw marquee box in a desired shape and click the start point again the complete the Lasso Selection. - The selected Patterns will be highlighted in yellow. - Similar with selecting Patterns with the marquee box, Patterns should be fully enclosed. Select Multiple Patterns - While selecting Patterns, hold down the Shift key and select all Patterns you desire to select. Move Pattern With Mouse - Click and drag the Pattern. With Arrow Keys - Click the Pattern to be moved. - Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the Pattern towards the desired direction. - The Pattern will move in 1cm increments when using the arrow keys on the keyboard. Move in Guidelines - While click and dragging the Pattern, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to activate the guidelines. - The Pattern can be moved in a straight line or a diagonal line. Scale Pattern Scale Manually - Click the Pattern to be scaled. The marquee box will appear around the Pattern. - Click and drag the white point on the marquee box to enlarge or shrink the selected Pattern. Scale with Specific Values - After selecting the Pattern and click and dragging the white point on the marquee box, right click on the 2D window. - The Transform window will appear. - Enter the desired values to Percentage and Dimension to scale the Pattern with the desired values. Rotate Pattern - Click on the Pattern to show the marquee box. - Click and drag the white point above the marquee box to rotate the selected Pattern. Pivot Point - The point at the center of the Pattern appears with the marquee box is the Pivot Point. - Double click the Pivot Point to activate it. - Move the Pivot Point to change the fiducial point which the Pattern will rotate on the basis of.

Title: Pressure
Content: List of Contents Pressure Set Pressure Pressure - Assign Pressure to Patterns to express inflated Garments/accessories such as padded jumpers, balloons, pillows, and cushions. - Navigate to the Property Editor Simulation Properties Pressure Set Pressure - Using the Transform Pattern tool, select the Pattern to be edited. - Navigate to the Property Editor Simulation Properties Pressure. - When the Pressure value is positive, the Pressure is applied to the back of the fabric, but when the Pressure value is negative, the Pressure is applied to the front of the fabric. - Assign values to Pressure so that the outside Patterns Pressure value is 10 and the inside Patterns value is -10. Be mindful that the absolute value for two Patterns should be the same. - When the Simulation is activated, the Patterns will inflate.

Title: Lock All Patterns
Content: Lock All Patterns - Lock all Patterns to inhibit selecting and editing in the 2D window and easily select and edit Internal Lines. - Right-click on the 2D window and select Lock All Patterns from the pop-up menu. All Patterns will turn grey and be deactivated. - Only activated Internal Lines can be selected and edited. Lock Selected Patterns_ver5.0.0 and Above - Select the Transform Pattern or the Edit Pattern tool. - Right click on the Pattern to be locked and select Lock Pattern from the right-click pop-up menu. - The selected Pattern and all Internal Lines within are locked and cannot be selected. - The selected Pattern and Internal Lines turn grey. - To unlock the Pattern, right click on the 2D window and select Unlock All Pattern Outlines.

Title: Focus Zoom
Content: Focus Zoom - Zoom to the selected Pattern and control the 3D window fiducial to the selected Pattern. - Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. Right-click on the Pattern or the object and select Focus Zoom from the pop-up menu. - Or, select the Pattern or the object and then hit the F key on the keyboard. - The 3D window will adjust automatically to zoom to the selected Pattern and the 3D window will be controlled based on the selected Pattern.

Title: Linear Garment Measure
Content: List of Contents Linear Garment Measure Create Measure Linear Garment Measure - Measure the length of the particular part of the 3D Garment. - Select the Linear Garment Measure tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment Measure Linear Garment Measure. Create Measure - To create a measurement, you need to click twice on the 3D Garment. - Firstly, click on the start point where the length of the 3D Garment should be measured. - Drag the mouse and click again on the end point to complete the measure. - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard while dragging the mouse in order to drag it in a straight line. - The measure will be highlighted in yellow when it is created properly.

Title: Edit Measurement
Content: Edit Measurement Edit Measurement Select Measurement Edit Measurement - Configure properties of a measurement or open, delete, and save a measurement. - Select the Edit Measurement tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Avatar Measurement Edit Measurement - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure. Select Measurements - Select the Edit Measurement tool from the 3D Toolbar and click on a measurement on the Avatar. - The selected measurement will be highlighted in yellow. Configure Measurement Properties - Navigate to and select Avatar Editor Measure to view the selected measurements properties. - The Name can be changed. - Choose the Measurement Type between the basic and the Surface. - The basic measurement uses the protruding areas of the Avatar as the standard whereas the surface measurement measures along the curvatures of the Avatar. - Check values for Measurement Information, Basic Length, and Surface Length. - Toggle on or off the SHOW option to show or hide the selected measurement from the 3D Window. Save Measurements - Navigate to and select Avatar Editor Measure. Select the Save icon on the right top of the Measure tab. - The Save File window will appear. - Locate the saving path, assign the file name, and select Save. - The measurements will be saved as a .mea file. Open Measurements - Navigate to and select Avatar Editor Measure. Select the Open icon on the right top of the Measure tab. - The Open File window will appear. - Locate the file to the opened and click Open. - The .mea file with measurements will open. Delete Measurements - Navigate to and select Avatar Editor Measure. Select the measurement to be deleted from the measurement list. - Click the Delete icon on the right top of the Measure tab. - Or, select the measurement in the 3D window using the Edit Measurement tool and hit the Backspace or the Delete key on the keyboard. - The selected measurement will be deleted.

Title: Delete All Curve Points
Content: Delete All Curve Points - Delete all curve points on a segment. - Select the Edit Curve Point tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment and select Delete All Curve Point from the pop-up menu. - All curve points on the selected segment will be deleted.

Title: [Property] Button Property Setting
Content: Objective Adjust button properties in the Property Editor. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Explanation Selecting a button with Select/Move or Select/Move Button tool displays its properties in the Property Editor. Button Property Description Angle Enter desired value for rotation angle of buttons. Thread Length (cm) Enter desired value for thread length in centimeter (cm) from the range of -1.00~1.00. Style Select a button style. Collision Set ON/OFF for collision option. Set it OFF in order to fix its location to avoid the collision between the buttons and the Patterns. 2D Measurements View the position of buttons in 2D Pattern with its size measurement. Set check-boxes On for Left/Right/Up/Down as desired. The 2D size measurements appear accordingly.

Title: Apply Buttonhole Style
Content: List of Contents Apply Buttonhole Style In Property Editor Select A Buttonhole And Apply Buttonhole Style Select A Buttonhole And Apply A New Buttonhole Style Objective Apply buttonhole styles or fabric material (.zfab) onto buttonholes as desired. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Operation Apply Buttonhole Style In Property Editor Click on a buttonhole and select a buttonhole style in the Property Editor. The selected buttonhole style is now being applied to the buttonhole. Select A Buttonhole And Apply Buttonhole Style Select a buttonhole. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Assigned to Selected Patterns The buttonhole style is now being applied to the selected buttonhole. Select A Buttonhole And Apply A New Buttonhole Style Select a buttonhole. Follow the indicated guideline: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Assigned to New Fabric A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.

Title: Arrangement Property Setting
Content: Objective Set arrangement property details once arranging patterns with Arrangement Points. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select 3D Pattern Property Editor Arrangement Note: The arrangement properties are only accessible to Patterns that are arranged by Arrangement Points. Operation Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select 3D Pattern Property Editor Arrangement Point Name Shows which arrangement point the selected pattern is on top of. Shape Style Changes the arrangement bounding volume pattern to be flat of curved. Position X Moves horizontally according to the arrangement bounding volume. Position Y Moves vertically according to the arrangement bounding volume. Offset Adjusts the offset and curvature between the arrangement bounding volume and the pattern. Orientation Changes the pattern's direction according to the arrangement bounding volume.

Title: Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points/Flip Wrap Direction
Content: Objective Arrangement Points are created on the basis of the Bounding Volume surrounding the Avatar, and are arranged on the Avatar according to the Bounding Volume's curves. Note: Precise arrangement is available by using Gizmo or Property Editor even after arranging with Arrangement Points. Location Avatar Display Show Arrangement Points Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Avatar Display Show Arrangement Points The Arrangement Points appear around the Avatar. Select a Pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point. A preview of the Pattern placement is being displayed (ver2.4.0). Select a desired Arrangement Point. The center of the Pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the Patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied (ver3.0.0). Note: Flip Wrap Direction Patterns that the length are longer than the Bounding Volume, such as cuffs, get arranged spiral. Right-click on patterns in the 3D window Click Flip Wrap Direction to flip its direction.

Title: Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment
Content: List of Contents Guideline for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment 1. Set up on Server PC 2. Set up on Client PC Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment Objective Set up CLO 3D/Marvelous Designer Network Version on the Internet environment. Note that you do not need to follow the set-up guidelines below when a Server PC and Client PC are under the same local network environment. Simply plugging the dongle key into a Server PC enables you to run CLO 3D or Marvelous Designer on any PCs under the same local network as the Server PC located without any extra settings. 1. Set-up on Server PC Operation Plug the dongle key in the Server PC and install the HASP Driver. HASP Driver gets automatically installed during the software installation. However if any trouble occurs during the process or in case of Server only being connected with the dongle key, HASP Driver should be installed manually. Guideline for Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. Make sure the local IP address of the Server is static. (Local IP is dynamically allocated Intranet IP by the router.) The local IP address gets changed when the router is restarted if the local IP is not set in static status. To avoid repetitive IP reset in the process, 'port forwarding', set your Server's local IP as 'static'. Port-forward Port 1947 for TCP and UDP of the Server's local IP in the router setting. Port-forwarding enables to transmit the data from Client/Server to Server/Client through Port 1947. Port-forwarding method varies considerably in the types of router therefore please ask for support from your network manager. Note: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding http://www.wikihow.com/Set-up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router 2. Set-up on Client PC Operation Run CLO 3D/Marvelous Designer Network Version installer. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and the dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. Set external IP of the Server on the dongle key configuration to let the software reaches the Server for an authentication. This can be done through Sentinel Admin Control Center which is automatically installed during the HASP Driver installation. Access to http://localhost:1947 Click on 'Configuration' (the red box) Click on the third tab called 'Access to Remote License Managers'. Make sure to check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote License' and to type the Server PC's external IP in 'Specify Search Parameters' (note that the external IP is different from the local IP mentioned in the 'Set-up on Server PC'). You are able to see the external IP of the Server PC on the website (http://www.whatismyip.com/). Go Back to the List of Contents

Title: Modify Piping Status
Content: Objective Modify Piping status. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Edit Piping Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Edit Piping Right click on a desired piping to edit. Piping pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu Definition Delete Delete the selected Piping. Refresh Piping Re-drape the selected Piping. Deactivate/Activate Deactivate/Activate selected Piping. Freeze/Unfreeze Freeze/Unfreeze selected Piping. Quadranglate Change Piping mesh to quads. Triangulate Change Piping mesh to triangles. Hide Hide selected Piping. Show All Piping Show all Piping.

Title: [Object Browser] Copy Button Style
Content: Objective Copy and modify a button in order to create a new button style or adjust its properties. Location Object Browser Button Tab Copy Operation Object Browser Select an item in the button tab. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Copy A new button item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.

Title: [2D Tool] 1:N Segment Sewing
Content: Objective Easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. Location Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar Segment Sewing Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. Note While establishing 1:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the sewing line cannot be applied. While establishing N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.

Title: 3D File (FBX) Import/Export
Content: List of Contents Import FBX Export FBX Objective By Importing an FBX file, Geometry, Material, Joint, Camera, and Camera Animation information are also imported Operation Import FBX / Import (Add) FBX Main Menu File Import/Import (Add) FBX The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. The Import FBX window appears. Select the settings and click OK. The FBX file is imported based on the setting. Basic Load Type Open or import the FBX file. Object Type Import the FBX file as Avatar or Trim. Scale Select the unit or enter the specific value. Object Camera Toggles whether the Camera data or Camera Animation data is imported. Animation Toggles whether the Animation data is imported. Cache Animation (MC) Toggles whether the Cache Animation data is imported. Axis Conversion (ver 7.3) Change the direction of each axis of the object. Option Move Garment to Start Position Jump to the position of the start frame of the motion where the garment was loaded and move it.. Note: Among the avatar skinning types, Dual Quaternion and Eblend are not compatible with CLO. Export FBX Main Menu File Export FBX The Save File window appears. Designate the file saving path and file name, and then click OK. The Export OBJ window appears. Select the settings as needed and click OK. The file is exported as a FBX file based on the setting. Object Select an Avatar Select the avatar to be exported. Note: The selected avatar is saved with its rigging data. You can exclude it as desired. Single/Multiple Exports selected objects as Single or Multiple Objects. Unweld/ Weld When exporting, the connected Vertex(Mesh's points) where seamlines are set in the pattern are combined into individual objects or a single point. Weld selected Patterns in Workspace Weld the selected patterns connected by sewing lines. Thin / Thick Sets whether to export geometry of the rendering thickness. Unified UV Coordinates (PNG) Exports the texture information of all garment patterns to fit within the UV coordinate values between 0 and 1. Image Scale Set image scales. Fill Texture Seams This Function expands the range of the texture based on the border of the texture. Include Internal Shapes The information of the Internal Line included in the garment is also exported. Option Animation When the FBX file is loaded, the animation information in the file is saved together. Cache Animation (MC) Save the recorded garment animation as cache data together. Basic Scale Enter a number or select the desired unit from "Unit of file to be imported" and adjust the scale of the object. Animation Entire Region Save the recorded garment's animation entirely. Play Region Only the garment animation in the play area is saved. File Type Select whether to save as Binary / Ascii. The file is stored in binary and cannot be opened by the user. Ascii: The file is saved as text so the user can open and understand it. Texture Relative Texture Image File Path Save only the texture name without the texture image path, so if the saved FBX file and the texture image used in the file are in the same path, the texture image is automatically loaded. Absolute Texture Image File Path Save the folder path where the texture image was located as the texture image path. If the path of the texture image is changed, the texture image cannot be loaded. Embed Media (.zip) Export as a zip file along with the texture files used. Diffuse Color Combined on Texture When a color is applied to the texture, it is saved as a combined color and texture. Note: FBX files cannot contain all data, texture images and color values so select that option to export color information applied to textures as well. File Save Colorways Export the garment with colorways

Title: Video Capture 3D Garment (Save)
Content: Objective Save recorded file as *.avi format. Location Turntable Video Capture Preview (Preview window that appears after the recording) Save Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Turntable Video Capture Preview (Preview window that appears after the recording) Save Save File window appears. Enter desired file name and location, then click Save button. The recorded file is now being saved.

Title: Move/Rotate Pattern with Gizmo
Content: Objective Move or rotate Patterns, objects, Avatar Joints and etc. with the Gizmo. Location Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard Note: Preferences for the Divided Gizmo can be accessed via: Main Menu User Setting 3D Gizmo Divided Gizmo Operation Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard The Gizmo appears. Move by dragging in a desired direction. Note: Move Y Axis Click &gt Drag the green arrow (pointing up) up and down to move the Pattern vertically. Move X Axis Click &gt Drag the red arrow (pointing right) left and right to move the Pattern horizontally. Move Z Axis Click &gt Drag the blue arrow (pointing forward) forward (upwards on the screen) or backwards (downwards on the screen) to pull or push the Pattern to the front and back. Yellow Square Box Free drifting to horizontal/vertical directions. Rotate Follow the indicated guideline below: Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard The Gizmo appears. Mouse over the Gizmo's rotation axis. The mouse cursor shape is now being replaced to (Rotate). Click Drag in the desired direction to rotate the corresponding object. Note: Rotate Y Axis Click &gt Drag the green radius left and right to rotate the Pattern centered on the vertical line. Rotate X Axis Click &gt Drag the red radius up and down to rotate the Pattern centered on the horizontal line. Rotate Z Axis Click &gt Drag the blue radius the Pattern with the central point as the axis.

Title: [3D Tool] Tack on Avatar
Content: Objective Temporarily fix a point of a Garment to an Avatar. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar Tack on Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar Tack on Avatar Click on a point of a 3D Garment to fix. A point is now being created and a dotted line follows along the mouse cursor, and the selected garment becomes semi-transparent. Click on a point of an Avatar. The selected Garment is now being opaque once again. Same tack is now being created in the corresponding 2D Pattern. Activate Simulate. The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to the Avatar.

Title: CLO-SET CONNECT LINK
Content: List of Contents Check Item and Purchase CLO-SET CONNECT Account Link Check Purchase Item Objective Check the sales and purchase products of CLO-SET CONNECT within CLO. Location Library CLO-SET CONNECT Operation Check Item and Purchase Select the tool/menu indicated. The parent category of CLO-SET CONNECT appears in the folder list. Check the desired purchase folder. Sales items appear. Click the item you want to purchase. Links to the detail page of the item. Proceed to purchase at CLO-SET CONNECT. CLO-SET CONNECT Account Link Select the tool/menu indicated. Click the Account at the top right. The Account window appears. By default, the CLO-SET CONNECT account is linked to the corresponding CLO account. If you want to link other accounts, log out from the CLO-SET CONNECT page. Again, click the Account Add Account in CLO. You will be taken to the CLO-SET CONNECT login page. After logging in with the account to be linked in addition, check CLO again. The account is added to the Account window. Check Purchase Item Select the tool/menu indicated. Click the My items folder. The folder with the linked account name appears. Click the folder. The purchased item appears. Click the purchased item to download. The item is activated and downloaded to the path below. Windows C: Users User Name Documents CLO Assets My Items

Title: Segment Topstitch
Content: Segment Topstitch - Establish the Topstitch along the Segments of the Pattern outlines and the Internal Shapes/ Lines. - Select the Segment Topstitch tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material Segment Topstitch. - Hover over the desired Segment of the Pattern outlines or the Internal Lines. - Click and on the Segment. - The Segment Topstitch created on the Pattern outlines or the Internal Lines should be highlighted in pink.
